shared_context.topic: hepatitis A IgM test result interpretation

snippets.output: A non-reactive result for the hepatitis A IgM (anti-HAV IgM) test indicates that the individual does not have an acute hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection.
IgM antibodies are typically present during the acute phase of hepatitis A infection.
IgM antibodies usually appear shortly after the onset of symptoms of acute hepatitis A infection.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single-atom standalone fact about IgM timing.

snippets.output: In acute hepatitis A infection, hepatitis A IgM antibodies peak within the first few weeks of infection and then decline over the next few months.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel temporal facts about IgM kinetics (peak + decline).

snippets.output: A non-reactive hepatitis A IgM result suggests that the person has never been infected with HAV.
A non-reactive hepatitis A IgM result suggests that any previous acute hepatitis A infection has resolved to the point where the IgM antibodies are no longer detectable.
In cases where acute hepatitis A infection is strongly suspected but initial anti-HAV IgM results are non-reactive, retesting may be considered.

In cases where acute hepatitis A infection is strongly suspected but initial anti-HAV IgM results are non-reactive, retesting may be considered if the clinical presentation is consistent with hepatitis A.
Anti-HAV IgM may not be detectable at very early stages of acute hepatitis A infection.
If the hepatitis A IgM test was nonreactive, repeating the hepatitis A IgM test after some time can help confirm acute hepatitis A infection if the initial test was conducted too early.
